evidence: SummitPost lists the Northeast Couloir (via Magic-Pelton Col, couloir on rock or snow to the summit) as Class 3; climb/ski reports give 40-45 degree snow with brief 50 degree edges, booted, no ice.
note: Steep snow with no ice grade; SummitPost's own Class 3 agrees with the brief's steep-snow mapping.

evidence: SummitPost route list: Southwest Cirque, 'heathery gullies at the N or NE head of the cirque' to the summit ridge, rated 'Class 3-4'; top of range taken.
note: One route-specific rating (SummitPost, read via search snippets; the page 403s). A South Ridge trip report on the same summit ridge called that line 'class 3'.

evidence: MP: 'Moderate Snow, Grade II'; its direct line is 'moderate to steep snow; may have AI2+ ice'. SummitPost: several pitches of snow and ice to 60 degrees, Grade II.
note: The crux depends on conditions. In a snowy year it is moderate to steep snow: a Mountaineers party found 'a snow climb rather than an ice climb' and placed 2 screws and 2 pickets. MP's AI2+ is for the direct line when icy. AI2 is kept as the face's graded ice. Commitment II agrees with the sources.

evidence: The only route-specific account (WTA 2024): follow the Massie Lake High Route east, turn uphill for 'Massie Peak's west ridge', traverse the ridge a little over a mile and climb the peak. Gear: 'helmet, microspikes'; done with a dog 'with guidance'. No class number anywhere.
note: Tried Peakbagger (403), Peakery (no logs), ListsOfJohn (403), NWHikers (blocked), SummitPost Massie Lake pages (403), WTA and Wenatchee Outdoors. The dog-assisted ascent suggests Class 2-3. The record's top-of-range Class 3 is kept.

evidence: Mazamas 'Gunsight Peak, SW Face': 'A 5.6 rock climb', citing Beckey's Cascade Alpine Guide. CascadeClimbers thread: 'Beckey lists the SW face of the main peak as a sustained 5.6'. Wildsnow: about 5 short pitches, a loose blocky start, then 'wonderful easy climbing up cracks and knobs' on the ridge.
note: Middle Gunsight is the main (highest) Gunsight summit, and Beckey's SW line there is 5.6. No source gives a separate number for a 'SW ridge' apart from that line. The CascadeClimbers pages could not be read directly (search snippets only).
identity: This is very likely the same line as the peak's Standard Route (Beckey's SW face, 5.6), which is already in the catalog. Also check that area_id wa_middle_peak is Gunsight's Middle Peak and not the other Middle Peak by the Canadian border.

evidence: MP's grade string is 'Easy 5th ... WI1 PG13', but its text says the line avoids 'class 5+ scary cliff downclimbs'. Trip reports describe loose moraine, boulder fields, the Klickitat Glacier crossed in microspikes and 'steep, chossy, and crumbling' rock. None mention roped or ice climbing, and none give a class.
note: Not a summit route. Class 3 is inferred from the terrain; no source gives a class. MP's WI1 / Easy 5th string matches nothing on the normal loop. The record's discipline 'ice' is also wrong for an off-trail loop.

evidence: Swayne's first-hand account of the 1961 first ascent with Ed Cooper: three belayed pitches up the rightmost chimney in 'rotten ice, verglas, and snow', stemming the four-foot chimney and cutting holds, then crampons on the easier upper glacier. Wikipedia: Grade IV, 4-5 pitches of mixed climbing at about 55 degrees.
note: No source gives an ice or YDS grade. Mapped to Class 3 under the brief's rule for belayed steep snow. But this is a mixed chimney with ice and rock, so AI2 or low-5th mixed would be just as defensible. MP's 'Wilson Headwall' is the Rainier route.

evidence: SummitPost: several pitches of steep snow and ice ('three 50 meter ice pitches to the ridge crest'), Grade III. AAJ 1971: 60 degree snow/ice. Ski report: 'about 45 degrees for 600 ft'. Hebert kicked steps up the headwall. No source gives an AI grade.
note: Steep belayed snow/ice with no ice grade maps to Class 3 under the brief. The record's ice_grade AI3 is unsupported: nothing online grades this line, and MP's 'Park Glacier' (Mod. Snow, Grade II) goes around the headwall. If hard ice is the norm, AI2 is the most it would read.

evidence: AAJ 1975 (Markov party, first ascent): '1700 feet, NCCS II, F 6', 'a pleasant alpine scramble with two pitches of harder climbing on the steepest part of the ridge'. Beckey's description, quoted in a 2009 attempt report, matches but gives no number.
note: NCCS F6 = 5.6. The 2009 party turned back on moss and heather. The record's 5.7 has no source.

evidence: Abegg (2012 descent): 'grassy 3rd class ledges' with 'an occasional 4th class move' and 'one or two short 5th class downclimbing moves'; her partner rappelled. Beckey's one-line entry implies something easier (mostly Class 3).
note: Only one account, and it is a descent. Short 5th class with no number maps to 5.0 under the brief. The SummitPost Picket Range page, NWHikers, and the Lemke and Climber Kyle traverse pages were searched; none use this ridge.

evidence: Sources give only 'scrambling' for Dana, a Mountaineers Olympia boot-scramble peak. Mount Wilder, on the approach ridge, is 'class 2 South ridge', and Mount Barnes is class 2.
note: No route-specific class found: Peakery has no logs, and searches return the Sierra Mount Dana. The record's beta says 'class 2 scramble' but its rock_grade says Class 2-3, so the top of that range is kept. Class 2 may well be right.

evidence: From the Barrier notch: drdirtbag, 'Degenhardt's 4th class summit'. Chasingdonuts, following Beckey's 'obvious ledge behind the N skyline': 'The route could all be 3rd and 4th class to the summit', with a low 5th move only where they missed a bypass gully. Malclimbs: 30 minutes from the Barrier. Abegg calls the route low 5th, and a party that went off route roped up for about 5.7.
note: Two independent reports call the normal line 4th class; low 5th and 5.7 terrain appear only off route. Abegg's 'low 5th' holds this at medium.

evidence: The only mention is Beckey (AAJ 1967): 'In 1954 John Parrott and I climbed the ice apron and steep slabs of the direct northeast face', with no grade. The route lists on Wikipedia, MP and SummitPost do not include it.
note: No grade found for the 1954 face. 5.8 is the record's own value and has no support. The cascadecrusades 2011 report is a ski ascent of the East Face (50-55 degree snow, ice and rock), not this line.
identity: The record's beta ('Grade IV 5.5 ... 6-8 pitches of low 5th') describes the Northeast Buttress (Beckey-Stewart 1966), not the 1954 direct northeast face.

evidence: Mountaineers: 'a Class 4 route with a Class 5 step' across the east face ramps. MP and others call the loose-ramp/gully summit scramble class 4; the solid north-side alternative is 5.4.
note: A Class 5 step with no number maps to 5.0 under the brief. Sources split between 'Class 4' and 'Class 4 with a 5th step'. The record's breakdown '5.4 step' borrows the grade of the north-side variation.
